Assurance regime; jurisdiction US

Electrical and consumer product safety

Private manufacturer-paid certification ran for roughly ninety years before government accredited the certifiers; a 2007 incident wave made third-party testing mandatory for one product class.

Manufacturer picks and pays an accredited lab; OSHA and CPSC accredit the labs.

Payer, access, publication

Who pays. Manufacturer pays the testing lab.
Access. Samples submitted by the manufacturer; factory follow-up inspections.
Publication. Mark on product; test reports confidential; listings public.

1894voluntary assuranceUnderwriters Laboratories founded after electrical fires at the 1893 Chicago World's Fair; insurer-linked at origin.source
1903standardsUL publishes its first standard (tin-clad fire doors).2source
1972mandateConsumer Product Safety Act creates the CPSC.3source
1988accreditationOSHA Nationally Recognized Testing Laboratory program accredits third-party labs, ending single-lab dominance.3source
2007triggerLead-paint toy recalls.integrity_failure: Certified products found non-compliant; recalls of tens of millions of unitssource
2008mandateCPSIA requires third-party testing of children's products by CPSC-accepted laboratories.3source
